title: The Emitter Follower: Gain of One, Current to Spare
topic: BJT common-collector amplifier — output sits one V_BE below the input, so the voltage gain is about one, but the transistor delivers β times the input current; the canonical low-impedance buffer.

beats.narration: An amplifier with a voltage gain of one — what could that possibly be good for?

elements.content: Gain of one — yet every audio stage ends with one of these.

beats.narration: Drive the base, take the output off the emitter. The collector ties straight to V C C, and an emitter resistor pulls the emitter down to ground.

elements.content: NPN transistor centred; V_CC rail at top, R_E from emitter to ground
V_in source wire feeding the base
V_out tapped off the emitter node
V_in / V_out labels with arrows showing the path
common-collector — collector is the shared terminal

beats.narration: The base-emitter junction always drops about zero point seven volts when conducting. So the emitter voltage tracks the base — just shifted down by V B E.

elements.content: the output 'follows' the input — that's where the name comes from

beats.narration: Wiggle the input. The output traces the same wiggle, half a volt below it. Voltage gain is one — but the current swung into the load is beta times bigger than the current the source had to give.

elements.content: Time axis, voltage axis, two stacked traces V_in (chalk) and V_out (amber)
V_in sinusoid traces left-to-right with cursor
V_out tracks V_in, offset down by V_BE — same wiggle, lower DC
Live readout: V_out = V_in - 0.7 V as cursor sweeps
voltage gain ≈ 1, current gain ≈ β — the transistor delivers the muscle

beats.narration: High input impedance, low output impedance, current to spare — the emitter follower is the buffer that drives the speaker, the cable, the next stage.

elements.content: Hi-Z in, Lo-Z out — the buffer at the end of every signal chain.
